what_its_for: Zavegepant is used to treat migraine headaches in adults. It works by blocking a protein in the brain called CGRP that causes migraine pain and symptoms. It is used to treat a migraine attack when it happens — it is NOT used every day to prevent migraines.
how_to_take: Zavegepant comes as a nasal spray. To use it: 1) Blow your nose gently before using. 2) Hold the nasal spray device with your thumb on the bottom and your index and middle fingers on either side of the nozzle. 3) Tilt your head slightly forward. 4) Gently insert the tip of the nozzle into one nostril. 5) Press the plunger firmly all the way down with your thumb to release the spray. 6) Breathe in gently through your nose as you spray. 7) Remove the nozzle and breathe out through your mouth. Each device is a single-use, one-time-only spray — do not try to use it again after pressing the plunger.
dosing: The recommended dose is 10 mg (one nasal spray) into one nostril at the start of a migraine attack. You should only use one spray per migraine attack. Do not use more than one dose in a 24-hour period. Do not use more than 8 doses (sprays) per month.
missed_dose: Zavegepant is not taken on a regular schedule, so there is no 'missed dose' to worry about. Use it when your migraine starts. If your migraine comes back after getting better, do not take a second dose — wait until your next migraine attack.
storage: Store zavegepant nasal spray at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in the original packaging until you are ready to use it. Protect it from light. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them down the drain unless the instructions say to do so.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating or drinking for at least 1 hour after using zavegepant, as food and drink can reduce how well the medicine works. Avoid using other nasal sprays or nasal decongestants right before or right after using zavegepant without asking your doctor first. Tell your doctor about all medications you take, as some drugs that block a liver enzyme called CYP3A4 (such as certain antifungals or antibiotics) may increase zavegepant levels in your body.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you have: serious allergic reaction symptoms such as swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, trouble breathing, or a severe skin rash. Also call your doctor if: your migraines are not improving with this medication, you are using more than 8 doses per month, you experience unusual nasal irritation, nosebleeds, or discomfort in your nose, or you have any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Zavegepant starts working fairly quickly. Many people feel relief from migraine pain within 2 hours of using the spray. Some people may notice improvement even sooner. Results can vary from person to person.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not known if zavegepant is safe during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor before using this medication if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Liver problems: If you have severe liver disease, your doctor may need to adjust your treatment plan. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is needed for most people with kidney problems, but tell your doctor about any kidney issues you have. Elderly patients: Zavegepant can be used in older adults; no special dose change is needed, but always follow your doctor's instructions.
